executive_assessment.text: NDC reports 134.7 mm annual rainfall, 21 heatwave days yearly, and heatwaves lengthening 8 days per decade.
Recent heatwaves affected health of children and older people, livestock, crops, and infrastructure.
NDC’s 2030 adaptation priorities include agriculture/livestock, water, coastal zones, gender, and regional coverage.

geographic_notes.text: rural Djibouti: The NDC says rural women’s work burden rises as water, firewood, and pasture journeys lengthen.

rural areas; Djibouti City outskirts; regional centers: The NDC warns climate effects may worsen land degradation and poverty for pastoralists and small agro-pastoralists; livelihood losses may prompt movement to city outskirts.

Djibouti City: The CCDR summary reports single-event urban flood damages in Djibouti City up to US$43 million and projects annual flood damages +US$10 million and sea-level losses +US$38 million by mid-century.

known_gaps.text: The revised 2025 NDC is available in French; paraphrases were made from the French text, and local climate projections are not disaggregated by region in the cited passages.
The World Bank CCDR full report and model assumptions were not retrieved; its summary does not provide uncertainty ranges for the stated urban and livelihood estimates.
The NDC reports a risk of rural livelihood-driven movement toward urban peripheries, but does not establish conflict, violence, or measured migration outcomes.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
